--- name: workout-tracker-generator description: > Generate a complete, customized single-file HTML workout tracker app for a specific person. Use this skill whenever the user says things like "generate a workout tracker", "create a workout app for someone", "make a customized tracker", "generate the HTML app", "new tracker for a viewer", or mentions wanting to create a personalized workout tracker. Also trigger when the user provides fitness stats (body weight, body fat %, training experience) and wants a program built around them, or when they say "run the generator prompt". This skill handles the full flow: intake questions, program design, and complete HTML generation. --- # Workout Tracker Generator You are generating a complete, single-file HTML workout tracker app customized to one person's situation. The app runs entirely in the browser with zero dependencies — no server, no accounts, no build step. It's designed for phone use at the gym. ## How This Skill Works There are three stages: 1. **Ask intake questions** to understand the person's body, goals, experience, and constraints 2. **Design a periodized training program** based on their answers 3. **Generate the complete HTML file** by customizing the template The template file lives at `references/workout-tracker-template.html` relative to this skill directory. Read it before generating — it contains the full UI layer (CSS, HTML structure, rendering engine, state management, timers, export/import, dark mode, etc.) that you must preserve unchanged. You only customize the data structures and configuration described below. ## Stage 1: Intake Questions Ask all of these before generating anything. Be conversational, not clinical. Group them naturally. Where options are listed, present them as a selectable list so the user can just pick rather than type. The user can always add a custom answer if none of the options fit. ### Identity 1. **First name** — used in the app title and header (user types this) ### Body Composition 2. **Current body weight** — user types a number in lbs or kg 3. **Do you know your current body fat percentage?** Options: - Yes — I've had it measured - Yes — it's a rough estimate - No — I don't know it If YES: ask what it is and how it was measured (options: DEXA scan / Calipers / Smart scale or bioimpedance / Visual estimate). If NO: ask them to pick the closest description of their current build: - Significantly overweight — starting from scratch - Carrying extra fat but some muscle underneath - Average build — not lean, not overweight - Fairly lean but want more muscle - Already lean — focused on performance or size 4. **What's your physique goal?** Options: - Visible abs and a lean athletic look - Athletic and strong — not necessarily shredded - Just healthier and stronger than I am now - Bodybuilder lean / stage-ready - Specific body fat % target (user types it) ### Training Background 5. **How long lifting consistently?** Options: - Never — complete beginner - Less than 6 months - 6–12 months - 1–3 years - 3+ years 6. **Days per week to train?** Options: 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 / 6 7. **Session length?** Options: 30 min / 45 min / 60 min / 75 min / 90 min ### Equipment & Access 8. **Where do you train?** Options: - Commercial gym (full equipment) - Home gym - Limited equipment (hotel, apartment gym, etc.) 9. **Equipment you DON'T have access to?** Multi-select: - Cable machine - Squat rack / power rack - Barbell - Pull-up bar - Leg press - Machines in general (dumbbells only) - I have access to everything - Other (user types) ### Priorities & Limitations 10. **Muscle groups to prioritize?** Multi-select: - Arms (biceps + triceps) - Shoulders - Chest - Back - Glutes - Legs overall - Core / abs - No specific priority — balanced program 11. **Injuries or exercises to avoid?** Multi-select: - Shoulder issues (pain with overhead or pressing) - Lower back issues (pain with deadlifts or heavy bending) - Knee issues (pain with squats or lunges) - Wrist / elbow issues - None — I'm healthy - Other (user types details) 12. **Asymmetries to address?** Options: - One arm is noticeably weaker/smaller - One leg is noticeably weaker/smaller - No noticeable asymmetries - Other (user types details) ### Nutrition 13. **Rough daily calories?** Options: - Yes, I know roughly (user types the number) - No idea — and that's fine 14. **Do you track protein?** Options: - Yes (user types grams per day) - No 15. **Gender** Options: Male / Female 16. **Height and age** — user types both ## Stage 2: Program Design Design a phased training program based on their answers. The two big forks are whether the user knows their body fat percentage and their training experience level. ### BF% Known vs Unknown **If BF% is known:** - Design phases with specific BF% targets (e.g., "Cut from 28% to 20%", "Bulk from 20% to 24%") - Phase labels include BF% targets: `"Cut → 20%"`, `"Bulk #1"` - `phaseOverview` entries use `bfRange` (e.g., `"28% → 20%"`) - Exit criteria reference DEXA scans or BF% milestones **If BF% is NOT known:** - Design phases around training goals and timelines: "Foundation", "Strength Builder", "Growth Phase", "Lean Out" - Phase labels are goal-based: `"Foundation"`, `"Build"`, `"Lean Out"` - Do NOT reference BF% numbers anywhere — no phase labels, overview data, or rules should mention them - In `phaseOverview`, replace `bfRange` with a goal description like `"Build foundational strength"` or `"Reduce body fat while preserving muscle"` - Exit criteria are time-based and performance-based (e.g., "Complete 12 weeks OR when all compound lifts plateau for 3+ sessions") ### Experience-Based Programming **Beginners (<6 months):** - 3 days/week, full-body or upper/lower split - 2-3 phases over 6-9 months - 8-12 sets per muscle per week, rep ranges 8-15 - Mostly machines and dumbbells — focus on learning movement patterns - Longer rest on compounds (2-3 min) **Intermediates (6 months - 3 years):** - 4 days/week, upper/lower or push/pull/legs - 3-4 phases over 12-18 months - 12-16 sets per muscle per week - Mix of compound and isolation movements **Advanced (3+ years):** - 4-6 days/week with specialization - 4-5 phases over 18-36 months - 16-22 sets per muscle per week - Full exercise variety with weak-point work, planned deloads ### Nutrition Calculations Use Mifflin-St Jeor for BMR, then: - **Cut:** BMR x 1.4-1.5 activity multiplier, subtract 400-500 cal (never below BMR) - **Bulk:** TDEE + 250-400 cal surplus - **Maintenance:** TDEE +/- 100 cal - **Protein:** 0.8-1g per lb bodyweight (higher end during cuts) ### Exercise Selection - Order exercises by equipment location to minimize gym wandering — note the path in day subtitles (e.g., "Bench → Cable → DB rack") - Every exercise needs: `name`, `sets` (format: `"4×8-10"`), `rest` (format: `"90s"` or `"2 min"`), `notes`, `muscles` array, and `compound: true` if applicable - Include a swap alternative for every exercise in `swapMap` - Muscle tags must use these exact strings: `"chest"`, `"shoulders"`, `"triceps"`, `"biceps"`, `"back"`, `"rear delts"`, `"quads"`, `"glutes"`, `"hamstrings"`, `"calves"`, `"core"` - Notes should include practical gym-floor info: "same cable", "move to leg press", "same bench, lighter DBs" - For asymmetries, add notes on relevant unilateral exercises (e.g., "Right leg emphasis") ## Stage 3: Generate the HTML Read the template at `references/workout-tracker-template.html` relative to this skill's directory. The template is a complete working app (~1572 lines). You customize only the data structures listed below. Everything else — CSS, HTML structure, rendering, state management, timers, export/import, dark mode, scroll preservation, history, volume tracking, backup reminders — stays exactly as-is. ### What to Customize **1. Title and header:** ```html {Name} — Workout ``` In the body, find the `

` tag and update: ```html

{Name} Workout

``` **2. `phases` object** — the main exercise data: ```javascript var phases = { 1: { name: "Phase 1", label: "Foundation", color: "#2D6A4F", days: { "Mon: Upper": { subtitle: "Chest + Shoulders + Arms | Bench → Cable", exercises: [ { name: "Exercise Name", sets: "4×8-10", rest: "90s", notes: "Practical note", muscles: ["chest","shoulders"], compound: true }, ]}, }}, }; ``` **3. `phaseOverview` object** — phase detail panels. Each phase needs these fields: `title`, `goal`, `duration`, `calories`, `protein`, `bfRange` (or goal description if no BF%), `weightTarget`, `rate`, `training`, `activity`, `cycle`, `targetSets`, `rules` (array of strings), `exitCriteria`, `milestone`. **4. `phaseReminders` object** — brief per-phase reminders shown during workouts. Keep to one line with bullet separators: ```javascript var phaseReminders = { 1: { title: "Phase 1 Reminders", text: "RIR 1–2 every set • 13–15k steps • Refeed 1x/week" }, }; ``` **5. `swapMap` object** — every exercise in the program must have an entry mapping to one alternative: ```javascript var swapMap = { "Incline DB Press": "Incline Smith / Machine Press", "Barbell Back Squat": "Hack Squat / Smith Squat", }; ``` **6. `getTodayIdx` function** — maps JavaScript day numbers (0=Sun through 6=Sat) to day tab indices. Must match the user's training schedule. If different phases have different day counts (e.g., 4-day for phases 1-3, 6-day for phase 4), handle both cases with a conditional: ```javascript function getTodayIdx(phase) { var dow = new Date().getDay(); if (phase == 4) { var m6 = { 1:0, 2:1, 3:2, 4:3, 5:4, 6:5 }; // Mon-Sat return m6[dow] !== undefined ? m6[dow] : 0; } var m4 = { 1:0, 2:1, 4:2, 5:3 }; // Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri return m4[dow] !== undefined ? m4[dow] : 0; } ``` **7. Phase colors** — use distinct, accessible colors per phase: - Green/earth tones for cuts: `#2D6A4F`, `#8D4004`, `#C62828` - Blue/purple tones for bulks: `#283593`, `#6A1B9A` ### What NOT to Change Everything in the template outside the data structures above. This includes all CSS styles and animations, the HTML structure, the rendering engine (`render()` and all sub-renders), state management (`loadState`, `saveState`, localStorage keys), set tracking and timer and check-off system, export/import/backup system, dark mode, scroll preservation, session timer, volume
